caption: Figure 8: Chain of thought prompting allows language models to better perform multi-step reasoning tasks such as math word problems.
description:
Figure type: Comparison of two prompting methods for language models.
Section 1: Two examples of math word problems are shown, one using standard prompting and the other using chain of thought prompting. The chain of thought prompting method provides a step-by-step explanation of the reasoning process, while the standard prompting method only provides the final answer.

Section 2: Standard prompting: Q: Roger has 5 tennis balls. He buys 2 more cans of tennis balls. Each can has 3 tennis balls. How many tennis balls does he have now? A: The answer is 11. Chain of thought prompting: Q: Roger has 5 tennis balls. He buys 2 more cans of tennis balls. Each can has 3 tennis balls. How many tennis balls does he have now? A: Roger started with 5 balls. 2 cans of 3 tennis balls each is 6 tennis balls. 5 + 6 = 11. The answer is 11.

caption: Figure 9: We analyzed 150 random GSM8K examples, and found that PaLM 62B makes reasoning errors on 45 of them. These were manually categorized into three general error types.
